gloss: Raw worship a living mage contributes before saturation. One mage is the unit the other two classes are priced against.
Extra raw worship while a mage is blessed. Half a mage again, because a visibly favoured scholar is evidence of the god rather than a second scholar.
Ceiling of the mage class. Lowered first when worshipSnowball exceeds its threshold.
Raw mage input at which the class yields half its cap — about fifty mages. Raised second in the worshipSnowball retune order.
Raw worship a completed university contributes. An unfinished one contributes nothing at all.
Ceiling of the university class.
Raw university input at which the class yields half its cap — about ten completed universities.
Raw worship one member of the populace contributes. Small on purpose: the populace is the most numerous class and would otherwise dominate the sum before saturation could bite.
Ceiling of the populace class.
Raw populace input at which the class yields half its cap — about a thousand heads.
The sum of the three class caps, restated so the loader can check it rather than trusting arithmetic done by hand. It is a property of the formula, not a clamp applied afterwards.
Fraction of the gap to the target closed per world tick while worship is rising — about 5%, so devotion takes about twenty years to settle.

The same while worship is falling — about 15%. Strictly greater than the rise rate: a setback is felt in about five ticks and takes about twenty to earn back, and that asymmetry is the loop's damping.
The first geometric tier threshold. Tier t is reached at base × 2^t, so the thresholds are 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, 8192 against a ceiling of 9216.

How many thresholds exist, giving tiers 0 through 5 and an edict budget of 1 + tier that reaches 6 against EDICT_BUDGET_MAX = 8. The count is NOT a tuning knob — the observation's shape depends on it.
Favor a universe regenerates per world tick with no worship at all. Non-zero deliberately: a zero floor makes a bad start unrecoverable and produces long, uninformative Monte Carlo runs.
Favor per unit of worship per world tick. With the ceiling above, a maximally worshipped universe regenerates 5.5× a bare one. Lowered third in the worshipSnowball retune order.
The favor pool's ceiling at worship tier 0. The cap is what converts a worship lead from power into tempo — a high-worship god cannot do more things, only sooner.
How much each worship tier adds to the cap. Lowered fourth and last in the worshipSnowball retune order.
World ticks between decrements of an axis's recent-change counter — five world years.

Added to the cost multiplier per outstanding change on that axis, so the second flip inside the decay window costs double and the third triple. An escalating price rather than a lockout: a price is a gradient an agent sees in the affordability mask, a lockout is a hidden timer it has to learn to model.
How long a forbidding shock holds the worship target down — two world years.
The strongest a forbidding shock may be: the worship target is at worst halved. Forbidding an axis nobody uses lands near fp(1024) and costs nothing.
The tradition-change shock factor — the worship target quartered. A decade of ruin is the mechanical form of vision §4a's 'throws the civilization into upheaval'.
How long the tradition shock holds — ten world years, five times a forbidding.
A blessing's contribution to the shared research-rate channel. An existing primitive, not a new one: an effect the ablation sweep cannot see is an effect winRateByPrimitive cannot attribute.
A blessing's contribution to the shared teach-rate channel.
A blessing's contribution to the shared lifespan channel, in months, for as long as it lasts.
How long a blessing lasts. Re-blessing refreshes this rather than stacking the magnitude.
A fresh encouragement's contribution to one cell's research-rate, into the same (1 + Σ) channel and the same cap as every other source.
How much of that magnitude drains away each world tick. At fp(256) and fp(4) an emphasis lasts 64 ticks and then the slot is free.
How many cells may carry a non-zero emphasis at once. A bound, not a budget: the fourth encouragement is masked rather than displacing one.
Mastery a founding grant arrives at — full, so the recipient can teach it without loss. A grant at the research default would sit below the teach threshold and never leave the founder's head.

buildProgress one funding action buys, so four fundings complete a university. Invented here: §1.4 gives a university buildProgress and no content field supplied a rate, because funding is god action 11 and the god had no verbs.
What action 11 costs with a target of 0. Separate from the fund cost because §4.2 gives founding and funding one action id and they are not the same purchase.
Student seats a newly founded university will hold once complete. Invented for the same reason fund-progress is.
No ascension may be declared before this — fifty world years. The floor against a rush that would make the ascension band measure content rather than play.
Worship tier Path A requires. The first knob turned when ascensionRate leaves its 5–20% band.
Consecutive passing era boundaries Path B requires. The second knob in the ascension retune order.
The libraryDependence a passing era boundary must be at or below — 25%. The third and last knob in the ascension retune order.
Nodes that may leave the universe during a passing era, as a floor. The scale-relative allowance in ascension-loss-fraction takes over once the canon is large enough for a share of it to exceed this.

Permitted cells that must stand at their floor for Path A — deepest node held by a living mage. §8a's summit is 'the deepest node of a cell'; this is how many at once, and it is the conjunct that reads play. Calibrated, not guessed: the v1 rectangle is twelve cells and an unattended universe masters all twelve, so the tuner measures 12 infeasible (exploit −0.542) and 13 feasible (+0.167) — the first value needing an axis the universe did not start with. Set to 1 to recover the shipped rule.

Surviving instances a mastered cell's deepest node needs. Two is the shipped value, promoted from a literal in the rules to data: by construction only one mage has ever held a cell's deepest node, so a second copy is what makes teaching or scribing a necessary step rather than a nicety. Raise it once redundancy costs something.

Nodes a passing era boundary must hold — the 'knowledge' in §8a's 'held its knowledge intact across enough eras'. Before this the predicate asked only that nothing had gone wrong, so a universe nobody touches was a perfect custodian. Anchored to the passive baseline: the v1 rectangle holds exactly 51 nodes and an unattended universe learns all 51, so 51 is content exhaustion. 77 is 1.5x it. A count, not a fraction of the graph, so the summit cannot recede as content grows.

Distinct cells a passing era boundary must hold at least one node in. The spread half of 'its knowledge': a canon of the right size crammed into three cells is depth, and Path A already rewards depth. Anchored to the same passive baseline of twelve cells, at the same 1.5x. Set it to 0 to recover the predicate exactly as it shipped.

Share of the canon a passing era may lose — 5% — floored by ascension-loss-max. An absolute cap over a quantity that scales measures scale rather than custodianship: measured on this build, a passive universe holds 51 nodes and loses none while a broad one holds 220 and loses seven, so a flat allowance of two disqualified the civilization that was doing something and waved through the one in stasis. Set it to 0 to recover the predicate exactly as it shipped.
Consecutive world ticks with no living mage before the run ends as stagnated.
Worship below which the slow-death clock runs.
Consecutive world ticks below that floor before the run ends as stagnated — twenty world years.
Consecutive world ticks with no node newly entering the universe before the stasis trigger fires — but only while worship is simultaneously below the health floor.

The worship the stasis trigger is conjunctive on. A perfect custodian with a completed graph acquires no new nodes either, and terminating it as ruin would execute Path B's best players at tick 480 for a path that qualifies at tick 960. Stagnation must mean decline, not completion, and only worship separates the two.
The most one run may earn. With the retention below it fixes the carry-over's analytic limit.
The fraction of carried prestige that survives into the next run — 75%. The recurrence prestige' = prestige × retention + earned converges, and its limit is the cap below.

earn-max ÷ (1 − retention). A property of the arithmetic, not an arbitrary clamp: an infinite streak of perfect runs approaches it and never exceeds it. The loader asserts the identity, so a retune that breaks the relationship fails the load.
What ascending is worth before the achievement terms.
What reaching the tick cap without ascending is worth.
What a ruined run is worth. Non-zero deliberately: a zero floor makes losing streaks spiral, which is runaway leaders wearing the opposite sign.
Per deepest node tier the universe ever reached.
Per era survived.
Per peak worship tier held.

The ceiling of the saturating prestige-to-legacy conversion. Half the maximum prestige already buys 83% of the attainable head start, so the back half of the prestige range is nearly worthless — the second damping stage in series.
The half-point of that conversion.
Knowledge instances a maximally prestiged universe may be seeded with, placed in a library where they are lootable and burnable like any other.
The deepest tier a seeded instance may be. A legacy that could seed the summit would be prestige buying the ascension condition.

25% of the median unaided universe's value at the reference tick. THE single knob prestigeAdvantage turns — if it reaches zero and the metric still fails, the model is wrong and gets redesigned rather than retuned.
The world tick the unaided baselines below are measured at — ten world years.

Placeholder for the median unaided universe's favor pool at the reference tick. A measurement that has not been taken: the first prestigeAdvantage sweep replaces it, and until then it is the pool cap, which is the honest upper bound.
Placeholder for the median unaided universe's materials stock at the reference tick — the reference scenario's starting stock, which the first sweep replaces with a measured median.
Placeholder for the median unaided universe's headcount at the reference tick — the reference scenario's founding population, which the first sweep replaces with a measured median.

Founding grants a god may make before the universe has discovered anything. 4096 is unreachable — the grid holds 300 nodes and only prerequisite-free ones in permitted cells are grantable — so at this build no budget is in force and action 8 behaves exactly as it always has. The number is deliberately inert: the balance sweep varies it per arm through the scenario, and the value that ships here changes only once a curve says which one to ship.

Nodes the mages discovered for themselves that earn one further grant. The god buys the right to seed again by the universe demonstrating it can grow unaided. 0 would mean a fixed allowance and no accrual at all, which is a legitimate arm of the experiment rather than a disabled feature. Moved by whichever budget arm separates permit-then-idle from permissive-breadth.

Ceiling on grants ever authorized — starting allowance plus everything accrued. A ceiling on what may be granted, never on what is held, so a frugal god keeps earning and a spent one is not refunded. Unreachable at this build for the same reason the starting allowance is.
